jurisdiction.name: Nigeria
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Nigeria has no AI-specific law: several AI bills, including a National AI Commission bill and a digital economy bill with an AI chapter, are pending in the National Assembly. The main binding rules touching AI are the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, which limits decisions based solely on automated processing, and the Data Protection Commission's 2025 implementation directive, which adds duties for AI and emerging technologies. National policy rests on the National AI Strategy published in September 2025 by the communications ministry and the national AI centre (NCAIR), backed by NITDA's AI roadmap and 2026 cloud and digital-infrastructure rules that require AI governance and risk management from infrastructure providers. Sector regulators add AI-relevant rules: the communications regulator's 2026 internet code of practice sets duties for deploying AI, the securities regulator governs robo-advice algorithms, the central bank sets standards for automated anti-money-laundering systems, and the consumer protection regulator has drafts on AI-generated content and AI in marketing. Lagos, Kaduna and Ogun have no published state AI instrument.
lead_institutions: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy
National Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 11 October 2026 and covers federal law, the federal government and ministries, regulators, and the three largest state AI hubs (Lagos, Kaduna and Ogun). African Union and ECOWAS instruments are shown through the regional files. Nigeria's AI bills have not been passed, so they are listed as leads. Two central bank documents are recorded as located only, and Lagos State's announced AI guidelines have not been published. Not yet verified from the official text: the full text of the two central bank documents.

instruments.summary: Nigeria's first national AI strategy, led by the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy after an April 2024 co-creation workshop and stakeholder review from July 2024 to January 2025. It sets the vision of Nigeria as a global leader in ethical and inclusive AI and organises 34 strategies under five pillars: foundational AI infrastructure, a world-class AI ecosystem, AI adoption and sector transformation, responsible and ethical AI, and a robust AI governance framework. Governance commitments include an AI Ethics Expert Group/National AI Ethics Commission, national AI ethical principles, an AI ethics assessment framework, an AI governance regulatory body and a national AI policy framework; it creates no binding obligations.

instruments.english_title: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 37 of 2023)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
instruments.publisher_name: National Assembly of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
instruments.current_status: In force. The Act states its commencement as 12 June 2023, the date of presidential assent; it was published in the Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette Extraordinary No. 119, Vol. 110, of 1 July 2023 (Government Notice No. 82, Act No. 37). The bill passed the Senate on 3 May 2023 and the House of Representatives on 24 May 2023 per the schedule to the Act. In May 2026 the National Assembly's joint ICT committees announced a legislative review of the Act, citing AI among the reasons, and a Senate bill to amend it (physical offices for social media platforms) passed second reading in March 2025; neither has amended the Act as of 2026-10-11.
instruments.summary: Nigeria's comprehensive data protection statute: it establishes the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, sets the principles and lawful bases for processing personal data, and imposes duties on data controllers and processors, including data privacy impact assessments for high-risk processing (s. 28), registration of controllers and processors of major importance, breach notification and cross-border transfer rules. Section 37 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, with exceptions for contract, written law and consent, and requires controllers to provide human intervention, the right to express a point of view and to contest the decision. Controllers must also tell data subjects about the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling (ss. 27 and 34).

instruments.english_title: General Application and Implementation Directive (GAID) 2025 under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023
instruments.current_status: Issued under the hand of the National Commissioner/CEO on 20 March 2025 (reference NDPC/NDP ACT-GAID/01/2025) pursuant to ss. 1(a), 6(c), 61 and 62 of the NDP Act; the PDF was uploaded to ndpc.gov.ng in July 2025. Article 3(3) provides that upon its issuance the Commission ceases to apply the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation 2019 as a legal instrument, without affecting anything done under it. A 19 September 2025 effective date reported by commentators is not stated in the Directive or on the NDPC site and is not recorded.
instruments.summary: Binding directive issued by the NDPC under the NDP Act 2023 that sets out how the Act applies, including registration and compliance-audit filing for data controllers and processors of major importance, DPO duties, lawful bases, DPIAs, breach notification and cross-border transfers (117 pp., 52 articles and 10 schedules). Article 43 requires controllers and processors deploying emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, IoT and blockchain to document technical and organisational parameters respecting the right not to be subject to solely automated or algorithmic decisions, privacy by design and child safeguards, to file them and a DPIA (assessing disparate outcomes and vulnerability indexes) with their compliance audit returns, and to test, retool and continuously monitor such tools or discard them for unmitigable privacy risk. Article 44 lets the Commission prioritise privacy-enhancing technologies, invites benchmarking against the UN resolution on AI, and requires organisations to refrain from AI systems that cannot be operated in compliance with international human rights law; automated decision-making also triggers DPIA and consent-record duties (Arts. 18 and 28), and Article 41 requires safeguards against profiling or algorithms that could lead to prejudiced outcomes.

instruments.current_status: Superseded. Signed on 25 January 2019 by NITDA under the NITDA Act 2007. instruments.summary: Nigeria's first general data protection regulation, issued by NITDA: it set principles of lawful processing, consent, data security, privacy policies, third-party processing contracts, foreign transfer rules, data subject rights and an administrative redress panel, and required annual data protection audits. It required controllers to inform data subjects of the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, with meaningful information about the logic involved, and gave a right to data portability where processing is automated. Replaced in practice by the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and the NDPC's GAID 2025.

instruments.summary: Ministerial strategic plan for 2023–2027 organised around knowledge, policy, infrastructure, innovation and trade. Its policy pillar commits the Ministry to formulate a National AI Strategy, with targets of a top-50 global ranking in AI readiness and adoption by 2030, over 50,000 AI-industry jobs and positioning Nigeria as a top-10 location for AI model training and talent. It is the plan from which the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy was mandated; it is not binding.

instruments.summary: NITDA's plan to become an AI-enabled regulator by integrating document-processing automation (machine learning and robotic process automation), generative AI for content creation and drafting of regulatory instruments, and agentic AI for management and cross-departmental coordination. It covers people, culture, content, process and technology pillars, technical requirements, required skills and an action plan, with executive sponsorship and implementation by the Reforms Coordination and Service Improvement Unit. It applies only to NITDA's own operations and is presented as a model for other public institutions.

instruments.summary: Technical guideline implementing the National Cloud Computing Guideline for federal public institutions, cloud service providers, data-centre operators and other suppliers, covering procurement, security and resilience operations, migration, data sovereignty and data-centre standards. It defines AI infrastructure providers and requires that where AI infrastructure is used for government and regulated-sector workloads, providers implement AI governance, AI risk management, security, monitoring, incident response and auditability measures, aligning where appropriate with ISO/IEC 42001 and NITDA AI governance instruments. CSP evaluation also weighs ethical data handling in AI and automated systems in line with the NDPA GAID.

instruments.summary: Establishes a national assurance, certification and continuing-oversight regime for data centres, cloud services, integration services, AI infrastructure and sovereign compute supporting public institutions, regulated sectors and critical information infrastructure. instruments.current_status: SEC rule executed on 30 August 2021 (part of the SEC's 'New Rules and Amendments executed 30 August 2021', listed on the SEC Rules and Regulations page) and made under the Investments and Securities Act 2007. No commencement date is stated in the text, so no commencement date is given. Not superseded as far as the SEC rules page shows; the Investments and Securities Act 2025 has since replaced the 2007 Act, and the rule's continuation under it was not checked.
instruments.summary: Binding SEC rule for capital market operators and others offering digital (robo) advisory services, defined as investment advice through automated, algorithm-based client-facing tools with little or no human adviser involvement. Section 6 ('Governance and Supervision of Algorithms') requires boards and senior management to oversee the client-facing tool, mitigate fault or bias in algorithms, approve algorithm design and changes, and staff the firm to develop and review the algorithms; robo advisers also need an annual independent technology audit, suitability controls and risk disclosures, with special conditions for fully automated advisers.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Nigeria's earliest binding sector rule on governance and testing of automated, algorithm-driven financial advice.

instruments.current_status: Dated 13 February 2026, signed by the EVC/CEO and issued 'as a Guidelines' under s.70 of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, applying to all licensees; it replaces the Internet Code of Practice 2019 (s.8.3 transition). The accompanying NCC Guidance Notes (February 2026) set a 90-day regulatory gestation period from publication and full compliance 180 days from publication; no single commencement date is stated.
instruments.summary: NCC code binding on Internet Access Service Providers covering open internet, cybersecurity and data protection, child online safety, unlawful content and online platforms. Section 5.4 ('Deployment of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies') requires providers to notify the NCC before deploying AI tools in network management or customer engagement (services affected, replacements, upgrades, timelines and sunsetting), to inform affected subscribers especially where non-human interfaces handle complaints, to protect network integrity, comply with the NCC Cyber Security Framework and avoid accessing consumer data without consent, and to be able to withdraw AI tools on regulatory determination; the NCC may issue further AI guidance and governance standards.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First telecoms-sector rule in Nigeria with explicit AI deployment obligations.

instruments.summary: Draft interpretive guidance under ss.17-18 of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018. Guidance Note No. 1/2026 says undisclosed AI-generated or materially altered content in commercial communications may be misleading or deceptive under ss.123-126 of the Act and sets expected practices: prominent disclosure of AI-generated content, no AI-generated fake testimonials, no deepfakes of real persons without consent and disclosure, internal review of AI content, and transparency for AI chatbots. The companion draft Consumer Protection Regulations presume exploitation of vulnerability where algorithmic profiling or automated decision-making targets vulnerable consumers.

instruments.summary: Draft FCCPC regulations on sales promotions in Nigeria, including digital promotions. Part V ('Artificial Intelligence and Automated Marketing') would require undertakings using AI, machine learning or automated tools for promotions, marketing or consumer engagement to register that use with the Commission, label AI-generated marketing content, keep AI chatbots and virtual influencers transparent, let consumers opt out of AI-driven marketing, keep two years of records on AI system design, data sources and decisions, and bear liability for misleading or discriminatory AI outcomes; a separate clause requires algorithmic offers, pricing and targeting to be transparent and non-discriminatory and lets the Commission demand the underlying logic.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Federal law, the National Assembly, federal ministries, regulators and the states of Lagos, Kaduna and Ogun were searched. No AI Act or deepfake law has been enacted, AI bills are listed as leads, and there was no material for procurement, cybersecurity, indices or international instruments. The central bank's documents, several Lagos State sites and the health regulators remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: Backfill run 2026-10-11 in four parts (G1 federal law via nass.gov.ng, naltf.gov.ng and NDPC; G2 federal government incl. ministry-level search, NITDA and NCAIR; G3 regulators SEC, CBN, NCC, NDPC, FCCPC, NAICOM; G4 top states Lagos, Kaduna, Ogun, 30-minute cap per PROTOCOL §6, finished in about 3 minutes with no state records). Run in parallel with MYS on separate branches. No interruption. The earlier strategy record was re-checked (title fixed, dated 2025-09 from the cover, issuer the communications ministry; supersedes the August 2024 draft); domain-named organisation dropped. AU/ECOWAS instruments are attached via the regional files. No AI Act or deepfake law enacted; AI bills (consolidated House AI bill, HB 2567, SB 731, the Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill with an AI chapter, NDPA amendment) are leads; nass.gov.ng publishes no Senate order papers or bill texts for the 10th Assembly and only ~100 House order papers (all searched). GAID effective date not stated in the text. Access: cbn.gov.ng PDFs 403 to curl and WebFetch (2 CBN records located only; dates from CBN's official circulars listing), commsinnovation.gov.ng unreachable (fmcide.gov.ng used), FMCIDE DPI framework PDF 500, most.lagosstate.gov.ng TLS mismatch/503, lagosstate.gov.ng and ogunstate.gov.ng script-rendered, aiguide.lagosstate.gov.ng expired certificate/503. Health regulators (NAFDAC, MDCN) not reached. procurement, cyber-security, index-readiness, international: no material found.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (narrative.review_notes): Two central bank documents could only be located because the bank's website blocked access, and Lagos State's announced AI guidelines have not been published.

leads.title: A Bill for an Act to Provide for Establishment of the National Institute for Artificial Intelligence and Robotic Studies Sciences Regulation Commission to ensure Proper Control of Usage of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Technology in Nigeria, Regulate the Development, Deployment, and use of Artificial Intelligence in Nigeria and for Related Matters (HBs. 143, 601, 942 and 1810)
leads.english_title: Consolidated House AI regulation bill (HBs 143, 601, 942 and 1810)
leads.note: Pending bill, not law. Sponsors: Hon. Sada Soli, Hon. Benjamin O. Kalu, Hon. Ademorin A. Kuye, Hon. Ibrahim Ayokunle Isiaka, Hon. Akin Rotimi. Listed for second reading on the House Order Paper of 3 December 2024 (No. 68, https://nass.gov.ng/documents/download/11167). Component bills: HB 143 (National Institute for Artificial Intelligence and Robotic Studies, Somolu, Lagos; first reading 18 July 2023) and HB 601 (National Artificial Intelligence and Robotic Sciences (Establishment) Bill; first reading 12 October 2023), per the House Bills Progression Chart (https://nass.gov.ng/documents/billdownload/11085.pdf); HB 942 (bill to ensure proper control of usage of AI technology, Hon. Sada Soli) listed for second reading on 12 March 2024 and 27 November 2024 order papers (https://nass.gov.ng/documents/download/11110, /11166). No later stage (committee report, third reading, Senate concurrence, assent) found in the House order papers published on nass.gov.ng up to 23 July 2026; bill text not published on nass.gov.ng.

leads.title: Nigerian Artificial Intelligence Bill, 2025 (HB. 2567)
leads.note: Pending bill, not law. Sponsor Hon. Ahmed Munir; first reading listed on the House Order Paper of Thursday 23 October 2025 (No. 35, third session, https://nass.gov.ng/documents/download/11215). No later stage found in the House order papers on nass.gov.ng; bill text not published there.

leads.title: National Artificial Intelligence Commission (Establishment) Bill, 2025 (SB. 731)

Not verified on an official source: nass.gov.ng publishes no Senate order papers or bill texts for the 10th Assembly (the only copy of the Senate order paper found is on a civil-society host). Promote or update once an official Senate record or bill text is located.

leads.title: National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, 2025
leads.english_title: National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, 2025
leads.issuing_authority: National Assembly (joint Senate and House committees on ICT); executive-backed bill of the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy
leads.note: Pending bill, not law as of 2026-10-11. Bill text on nass.gov.ng (https://nass.gov.ng/documents/billdownload/11219.pdf, 63 pp.) includes Chapter Five 'Regulation of Artificial Intelligence and other Emerging Technologies': Part XI ethical governance of AI (s. 63 principles, s. 64 obligations of AI agents, s. 65 classification of AI systems by ministerial regulation, ss. 66-67 regulatory agency functions and powers including suspension orders and civil liability of AI agents) and Part XII regulatory sandboxes and testbeds for AI. The National Assembly Library Trust Fund reported a joint public hearing and plans for third reading in November 2025 (https://naltf.gov.ng/digital-economy-bill-poised-for-presidential-assent/) and, on 22 June 2026, that the Senate ICT committee chair said the bill was in its final legislative stage (https://naltf.gov.ng/digital-economy-egovernment-bill-ndpc-frameworks/). House bill number reported as HB. 1599 (not confirmed on nass.gov.ng). No assent found; record as an Act once assented and gazetted.

leads.title: A Bill for an Act to Amend the Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023, to Make it Mandatory for Social Media Platforms to Have Physical Offices Within Nigeria and for Other Related Matters, 2025
leads.note: Pending bill, not law. Sponsor Sen. Ned Nwoko (Delta North); passed second reading in the Senate in the week of 18-20 March 2025 (https://naltf.gov.ng/senate-plenary-recap-march-18-20th-2025/) and had a public hearing before the Senate Committee on ICT and Cyber Security in July 2026 (https://naltf.gov.ng/senate-moves-to-compel-meta-tiktok-and-global-tech-giants-to-establish-physical-offices-in-nigeria/). Not AI-specific. Separately, the joint National Assembly ICT committees announced on 12 May 2026 a wider review of the NDP Act citing AI (https://naltf.gov.ng/national-assembly-initiates-review-of-national-data-protection-act/); no amendment bill text found.

Also found: a Lagos State AI Guide platform at aiguide.lagosstate.gov.ng ('STANDARD Framework'); on 2026-10-11 curl failed (expired TLS certificate) and WebFetch returned HTTP 503, so its content could not be checked.
